name: Walpole
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Wikivoyage's South West region page lists Walpole among its cities ('close to surf and forest') and DBCA's Walpole-Nornalup page names it as the park's base; visitors base themselves here for the Valley of the Giants and the tingle forest.
objection: Its draws (Tree Top Walk, Nornalup Inlet, Coalmine Beach) are separate candidates, so the town risks being a wrapper; the proposer should place it as a base/destination name rather than a spot beside its own attractions.

name: Mount Barker
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Mount Barker destination page (walking, wine, wildflowers; gateway to Porongurup and Stirling Range) and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany and South West itineraries route through it; a base visitors use for the two ranges and the wine region.
objection: No Wikivoyage article of its own and the town has little to see itself; if the Porongurup/Stirling Range spots carry the visit, it may only be a gateway at a low rank.

name: Bremer Bay
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Bremer Bay destination page (Bremer Canyon orca season, Fitzgerald River NP, beaches) and Wikivoyage Albany names it as the eastern end of the Rainbow Coast; it is the base for the orca trips and the east of Fitzgerald River NP.
objection: The headline (Bremer Canyon orcas) is an offshore cruise and seasonal (Jan-Apr); the town's own sights are beaches named in passing. The board page was read only through search results (the site blocks scripts).

name: Kojonup
reason: For: Australia's South West has a Kojonup destination page and Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany itinerary calls it a 'popular stop'; the town has The Kodja Place and the Military Barracks museum.
objection: Against: its one real draw, The Kodja Place, is a separate candidate, so the town would be a wrapper beside its own attraction (COVERAGE 'A town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw'); a service stop on Albany Highway rather than a base.

name: Katanning
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Australia's South West has a Katanning destination page and a 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' article; Wikivoyage's Perth to Albany calls it 'a major regional town'; it has several draws of its own (All Ages Playground, saleyards viewing platform, Premier Mill Hotel, miniature railway).
objection: A wheatbelt-edge service town most travellers pass through; the attractions are modest and some (saleyard auctions) are weekly.

name: Katanning All Ages Playground
reason: For: the Shire of Katanning's visitor page and Australia's South West's 'Top 10 things to do in Katanning' both single it out as an 'iconic', free attraction with giant slides and seesaws for all ages, a known road-trip stop.
objection: Against: it is a playground, close to the 'ordinary suburban park' negative benchmark; the shire's own page is not independent of the board; better as a reason in Katanning's bio than its own spot.

name: Albany Convict Gaol
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing (restored 1852 cell blocks, the town's main museum, open daily) and Visit Albany's heritage page both name it; a paid museum with an hour's visit.
objection: Small volunteer-run museum; overlaps in theme with the Museum of the Great Southern and Patrick Taylor Cottage nearby.

name: Residency Museum
reason: Duplicate of Museum of the Great Southern: the Residency building is the WA Museum's Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road (Visit Albany lists only the Museum of the Great Southern); keep as one under that name.
objection: Wikivoyage still lists 'Residency Museum' with the shark jaw and Eclipse lens; if the proposer treats the Residency as a separate building, it must not become a second spot for one museum.

name: Albany Wind Farm
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing ('worth a visit even if you are not into windmills': boardwalks, ocean views, cliff staircase, open daily, free) and Visit Albany's Quick Top 5 names it among the must-sees with the Gap and Stony Hill; the start of the Windfarm to Little Grove walk.
objection: It is infrastructure; the visit is a boardwalk and lookout of 30-60 minutes.

name: Brig Amity Replica
reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both describe boarding the full-size replica of the 1826 settlers' brig with volunteer guides; a distinct thing to do.
objection: Against: Visit Albany says 'the Amity is part of the Museum of the Great Southern site on Residency Road', so it may be part of a larger spot (rule 3); volunteer-staffed with variable hours. Either keep it as its own spot or fold it into the Museum of the Great Southern's bio.

name: Patrick Taylor Cottage
reason: Rules 1-2: Wikivoyage Albany See listing and Visit Albany's heritage page both name it as WA's oldest surviving dwelling (1832, wattle and daub), an 11-room cottage museum open to visitors with a pioneer collection and garden.
objection: Small volunteer-run house museum, a 30-45 minute visit with limited hours.

name: Dog Rock
reason: Quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE 'Include'): Wikivoyage Albany See listing names it, a granite boulder shaped like a dog's head with a painted collar that locals love; the kind of photo stop the app keeps.
objection: A 5-10 minute look beside a road near supermarkets; only one counted source.

name: Vancouver Arts Centre
reason: Rule 2: an arts venue and community arts hub (Wikivoyage: 'a focal point for all forms of the arts'), not a sight; Visit Albany's heritage and arts page does not list it (the Town Hall is now the flagship gallery).
objection: It is a heritage-listed 1887 cottage hospital with occasional exhibitions; if a guide named a permanent gallery there it could be reconsidered.

name: Mount Melville
reason: For: a summit with an observation tower ('the Spark Plug') and walk trails over Albany, Princess Royal Harbour and King George Sound; Lonely Planet carried a 'Mt Melville Lookout Tower' sight (seen in search only; the page now redirects).
objection: Against: no counted source could be opened (Visit Albany's walks and parks pages do not name it), reviewers report the upper stairs closed and trees blocking views; Mount Clarence and Mount Adelaide are Albany's promoted lookouts.

name: Quaranup Point Possession Trail
reason: For: Wikivoyage Albany Do listing names the 1.6 km walk from the old Quarantine Station to Point Possession, where Vancouver claimed WA for Britain; a real walk with a historic endpoint.
objection: Against: only one counted source, short, and not among Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks; no coordinates yet.

name: Albany Historic Town Trails
reason: Rule 3: a self-guided route linking 39 heritage places in central Albany is a way to see the town, not a place; it is covered by Albany itself (and Visit Albany's 'Landmarks and Laneways').
objection: Wikivoyage lists it as a Do; its individual stops (Convict Gaol, Patrick Taylor Cottage) are judged separately.

name: Albany Whale Tours
reason: A spot is a place, not an operator: this is a whale-watching and harbour cruise company; the place is King George Sound (a separate candidate).
objection: None of substance; whale watching itself belongs in the King George Sound / Albany text.

name: Middleton Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page leads with Binalup / Middleton Beach (year-round swimming, shark net, summer patrols, Ellen Cove Boardwalk) and Australia's South West's Great Southern itinerary names it; RAC's Albany beach guide too.
objection: A town beach; its name in Noongar (Binalup) may be the form to use.

name: Frenchman Bay
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page lists Frenchman Bay (calm swimming and snorkelling, BBQs, picnic area) and RAC's guide names it; on the way to Torndirrup.
objection: A sheltered local swimming bay; less of a draw than Misery Beach nearby.

name: Ellen Cove
reason: Duplicate of Middleton Beach: Ellen Cove is the southern end of Middleton Beach with its boardwalk and jetty (Visit Albany and RAC both describe it within Middleton Beach); keep as one under Middleton Beach.
objection: The Ellen Cove Boardwalk is named in its own right as a whale-watching walk; mention it in Middleton Beach's bio.

name: Goode Beach
reason: For: a sheltered Vancouver Peninsula beach; RAC's Albany beach guide names it as the access to Mistaken Island (walkable at low tide).
objection: Against: no counted source names Goode Beach itself as a place to go (Visit Albany's beaches page omits it); it is a residential suburb beach.

name: Muttonbird Island
reason: For: the visitor place here is Muttonbird Beach, which Visit Albany's beaches page lists (surfing, fishing, sheltered cove by Shelter Island) and RAC describes; keep it under that name if approved.
objection: Against: the candidate as named is the island, a reserve with no visitor use; the beach is 4WD-dependent for much of its length and mainly a local surf/fishing spot.

name: Betty's Beach
reason: For: RAC's Albany guide names Bettys Beach camping area (2WD access, direct beach access, 40 min east of Albany).
objection: Against: no counted visitor source beyond a motoring-club list; a fishing and camping beach used by professional fishermen in autumn; lean reject.

name: Nanarup Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Visit Albany's beaches page lists Nanarup Beach (surf, 4WD, sheltered swimming lagoon, Taylor Inlet waterbirds, BBQs) and RAC names it.
objection: Mostly a local surf and 4WD beach; the lagoon is a 15-minute walk.

name: Cheynes Beach
reason: Second-tier beach a source names: Australia's South West lists Cheynes Beach and Visit Albany's beaches page describes it (whale watching in winter, clifftop views, salmon run, wildflowers).
objection: Rough water, not for swimming; 50 minutes east of Albany and mostly a fishing/4WD beach.

name: Misery Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page and Visit Albany both feature it; named Australia's Best Beach by Tourism Australia in 2022, with a new viewing deck and beach stairs; a distinct beach in Torndirrup NP.
objection: None strong; it is inside Torndirrup NP, so the proposer should make sure the park and the beach are not duplicates.

name: Natural Bridge
reason: Duplicate of The Gap: DBCA and Australia's South West list one attraction, 'The Gap and Natural Bridge', reached from one car park and platform system; keep as one spot (The Gap and Natural Bridge).
objection: The arch is a distinct landform with its own pathway; if The Gap is not in the kept list, this one must be kept as 'The Gap and Natural Bridge' instead.

name: Blowholes
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page and the Torndirrup park page list it with its own 1.6 km return walk; Wikivoyage Albany names 'the Blowholes' among the park's sights.
objection: Spectacular only with a big swell; otherwise a short coastal walk.

name: Salmon Holes
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page ('one of the most photographed views on the Torndirrup Peninsula') and Visit Albany's national parks page name it; a lookout and beach of its own.
objection: Dangerous water (Visit Albany warns of rips); visitors mostly stop at the lookout.

name: Cable Beach (Albany)
reason: Rule 3: a rough fishing beach right next to The Gap and Natural Bridge (DBCA: 'swimming is not recommended', for experienced anglers); not a distinct draw for a visitor beyond the Gap.
objection: DBCA does give it an attraction page.

name: Jimmy Newells
reason: Rules 1-3: DBCA site page (100 m walk to a viewing platform over a calm 'secret' inlet) and Visit Albany's national parks page name it among Torndirrup's lookouts; a named guide stop, not an anonymous pull-out.
objection: A short stop (15-20 minutes); could be folded into Torndirrup's text.

name: Bald Head Walk Trail
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA trail page (12.5 km return across Flinders Peninsula) and Visit Albany's 10 Great Walks list it; a full-day hike.
objection: Within Torndirrup NP; ensure it is not duplicated with a 'Bald Head' or 'Flinders Peninsula' entry.

name: Stony Hill Heritage Trail
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: DBCA lists 'Stony Hill and Peak Head' (500 m loop, park's highest point, new all-access walkway, 360-degree views); Visit Albany's Quick Top 5 calls 'the views from Stony Hill' a must-see; Wikivoyage Albany names the Stoney Hill Heritage Trail. Name it 'Stony Hill'.
objection: A 20-30 minute loop within Torndirrup NP.

name: HMAS Perth Wreck
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: Visit Albany has a page for the Former HMAS Perth II Dive Wreck ('one of Australia's most renowned diving sites', scuttled 2001 in King George Sound); a permanent place divers travel for.
objection: Only certified divers can visit (via dive shops), so most visitors cannot do anything there; could be held to review if the owner wants land-reachable spots only.

name: Michaelmas Island
reason: Rule 2: a nature reserve island with no visitor access; seen only from Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.
objection: None.

name: Breaksea Island
reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island in King George Sound with no public access; seen from the Gull Rock lookouts. No counted source names it as a place to go.
objection: Its lighthouse history is notable but not visitable.

name: Bald Island
reason: Rule 2: an offshore nature reserve with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Chatham Island
reason: Rule 2: small offshore reserve island west of Walpole with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Eclipse Island
reason: Rule 2: lighthouse island with no public access, seen from Torndirrup's lookouts; no counted source names it as a place to go.
objection: Its lighthouse lens is displayed at the Museum of the Great Southern.

name: Seal Island (Albany)
reason: Rule 2: small reserve island in King George Sound with no access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Shelter Island
reason: Rule 2: Visit Albany says Shelter Island is a class 1A nature reserve (no access); the visitor place is the beach in front of it (see Muttonbird Island).
objection: None.

name: Saddle Island
reason: Rule 2: offshore island with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Gould Island
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (at 122.86 E, off the Esperance coast); in any case an inaccessible island named only by a Wikipedia category.
objection: None.

name: Green Island (Great Southern)
reason: Rule 2: small island with no visitor use; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Doubtful Islands
reason: Rule 2: offshore island group with no visitor access; only a Wikipedia category names it.
objection: None.

name: Gull Rock National Park
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page and Visit Albany's national parks page (high lookouts over King George Sound and the islands, Ledge Beach and Boiler Bay swimming, Mount Martin walk among Albany's 10 Great Walks); free day-use park. Keep as one spot with Ledge Beach as its visitor point.
objection: A small park popular mainly with locals; its single named site is Ledge Beach.

name: Ledge Beach
reason: Duplicate of Gull Rock National Park: Ledge Beach (with Boiler Bay) is the park's one visitor site and DBCA's only attraction for it; keep as one under Gull Rock National Park, pinned at Ledge Beach.
objection: If the owner prefers the beach name, keep Ledge Beach instead of the park, not both.

name: Hassell National Park
reason: Rule 2: DBCA says 'there are no facilities or visitor sites in this park... best seen from your vehicle'; a 550 m-wide strip along the highway.
objection: None.

name: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page (visitor centre, trails, lookouts, rediscovered Gilbert's potoroo and noisy scrub-bird) and Visit Albany (Baie des Deux Peuples Heritage Trail to the main beach); a distinct reserve with its own visitor centre.
objection: Little Beach, its headline, is a separate spot; the reserve must not duplicate it (pin it at the visitor centre).

name: Sinker Reef Beach
reason: Rule 3: a clifftop view at the end of a 2 km sandy 4WD/walking track inside Two Peoples Bay reserve; one DBCA page, part of the larger reserve.
objection: DBCA does list it with 'magnificent coastal views'; could be mentioned in the reserve's bio.

name: West Cape Howe National Park
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA park page and Visit Albany's national parks page (southernmost promontory of WA, cliffs, Shelley Beach, hang-gliding, Bibbulmun Track).
objection: Most of the park needs a 4WD; the 2WD visit is Shelley Beach and its lookout (keep the pins apart).

name: Shelley Beach
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page ('the most visited area in West Cape Howe National Park') and Visit Albany's beaches page (crescent beach, lookout, paragliding, campground). Keep as one spot including Shelley Beach Lookout.
objection: Not safe for swimming; overlaps the park entry, so the park and the beach need different pins.

name: Shelley Beach Lookout
reason: Duplicate of Shelley Beach: the clifftop lookout on the road down to the beach is the same stop (Visit Albany describes the lookout within Shelley Beach); keep as one under Shelley Beach.
objection: DBCA gives it its own page as WA's premier hang-gliding launch.

name: Torbay Head
reason: For: DBCA attraction page (named by Vancouver in 1792; DBCA calls it the southernmost point of WA) and Visit Albany notes West Cape Howe as WA's southern promontory; a 'southernmost point' is the kind of landmark people seek out.
objection: Against: reached only by 4WD or a long sandy walk, mostly seen from Shelley Beach; likely folded into West Cape Howe National Park.

name: Dunsky Beach
reason: Rule 1: named only in a DBCA gallery caption, with no attraction page; 4WD-only beach in West Cape Howe NP.
objection: None strong.

name: Waterfall Beach
reason: For: RAC's Albany guide gives it a section (secluded beach in Two Peoples Bay with a small waterfall onto the sand) and Visit Albany suggests it as a walk from Little Beach.
objection: Against: Visit Albany treats it as an extension of a Little Beach visit (part of a larger spot), no counted page of its own. Note: DBCA's 'Waterfall Beach' page is a different place in William Bay NP near Denmark, which the enumeration may have missed and should be judged on its own.

name: Point Ann
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage Fitzgerald River NP both name it (purpose-built whale-watching platforms, southern right whales calve June-October, Point Ann Heritage Trail, beach, 2WD camping); permanent place, seasonal phenomenon.
objection: Its headline is seasonal; outside June-October it is a beach and heritage walk in Fitzgerald River NP.

name: Whalebone Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA's own site page (exploreparks/site/whalebone-beach) names it as a scenic beach between rocky headlands, for fishing and walking; a second-tier beach a real source names keeps.
objection: Remote: reached only by 4WD when the track is open, otherwise on foot via the Hakea Trail; both counted sources are DBCA (not independent), and few visitors get there.

name: West Mount Barren
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Wikivoyage's Fitzgerald River NP page; a summit/ridgeline walk (about 2 h return) with sweeping park and coast views.
objection: None strong; overlaps the Barren Range entry, which should not also be kept.

name: Barren Range
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of West Mount Barren (and East Mount Barren): the range is a landscape seen along the park, and its visitable points are the individual peaks, kept separately.
objection: Wikivoyage lists the Barren Range as a See item in its own right; if neither Mount Barren were kept, the range would be the spot.

name: Quoin Head
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page calls it one of the park's most spectacular headlands, popular with photographers, with a bay, beach and campground; Wikivoyage lists its campsite.
objection: Remote, 4WD access; both counted sources are DBCA.

name: St Mary Inlet
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page names it (scenic inlet behind the dunes near Point Ann, birdwatching, shore walk at low water, campground). Case for: a named visitor site with a campground listed by Wikivoyage. Case against: rule 3, it sits beside Point Ann (the park's whale-watching point) and may be part of that visit rather than a distinct draw.
objection: No formal paths; the visit is mainly camping or a look on the way to Point Ann.

name: Hamersley Inlet
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (deep inlet in a winding valley, birdlife, beach, picnic and camping) and Wikivoyage lists its campsite; a second-tier inlet stop at the end of Hamersley Drive.
objection: One agency page plus a Wikivoyage camping line; a quiet place mostly for campers.

name: Hellfire Bay
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback. The DBCA page places Hellfire Bay in Cape Le Grand National Park (Esperance), not Fitzgerald River NP as the candidate note says.
objection: It is a strong draw in its own region; the golden-outback pass must cover it.

name: Hakea Trail
reason: Rule 1: named only as a DBCA gallery caption and as the foot route to Whalebone Beach; DBCA has no trail page for it (exploreparks /trail/hakea-trail 404). Case for: a coastal walk through the park's plant diversity linking Quoin Head and Whalebone Beach. Case against: one weak mention, and rule 3, it may be best folded into Whalebone Beach/Quoin Head.
objection: No length, trailhead or trail page found; a gallery caption is a thin source.

name: Hamersley Drive
reason: Rule 3 / 'a spot is a place': a road through the park named only in a DBCA gallery caption; its stops (Hamersley Inlet, East Mount Barren) are the places and are judged on their own.
objection: It is the park's main sealed scenic route and could carry a drive spot if the owner allows drives.

name: Mount Hassell
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page for a Stirling Range summit walk (moderately difficult, wildflowers, views to Toolbrunup); a real 2-3 h climb in the park. Location confirmed in Stirling Range NP (Great Southern).
objection: One counted source, and a lesser peak beside Toolbrunup; an owner could treat it as marginal.

name: Dillon Bay
reason: Re-looked: no counted source found (only ExplorOz, BeachSafe and campsite directories, plus Wikipedia's Bremer Bay page). Case for: a sheltered bay south of Bremer Bay with Blossoms Beach (4WD beach driving), camping and fishing, partly in Fitzgerald River NP. Case against: rule 1 fails without a visitor-oriented source; it reads as a locals' fishing spot.
objection: No tourism board, DBCA or guidebook names it; ExplorOz and BeachSafe are not counted sources.

name: Denmark Historical Museum
reason: Rule 1: one counted source, a Wikivoyage See listing (16 Mitchell St, local history of Denmark's timber and industrial times). Case for: open to the public, a half-hour indoor visit. Case against: a small volunteer local-history museum with limited hours; the friend test says only if nearby, and it needs a second source.
objection: Single source, short visit, local interest only.

name: Ocean Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found a counted source, Tourism WA's attraction page (westernaustralia.com/au/attraction/ocean-beach), plus Wikivoyage Denmark naming it as within cycling reach; Denmark's patrolled surf beach at the mouth of Wilson Inlet with a lookout, surf club and walks.
objection: Strong rips near the inlet; a beach mainly for surfers in cool water.

name: Denmark Wineries
reason: Not a place: a grouping of many cellar doors around Denmark; the winery rule keeps only an estate a visitor source singles out as a destination, and none is named here.
objection: Wine is a major reason people visit Denmark; that belongs in the destination description, not a spot.

name: Mount Frankland National Park
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. Wikipedia places the park in the South West region, and the neighbouring localities (North Walpole, Broke) are in the Shire of Manjimup.
objection: DBCA files it under Walpole and the boundary runs close; if the owner puts the line at Walpole's catchment, it is a clear keep (DBCA park page, summit trail and wilderness lookout, Walpole Visitor Centre names it). The south-west pass must cover it.

name: Walpole-Nornalup National Park
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA park page (tingle and karri forest, inlets, Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk, Hilltop, Bibbulmun Track) and the Walpole Visitor Centre's explore page; a flagship forest park.
objection: Most of its draws are separate candidates (Valley of the Giants, Giant Tingle Tree, Circular Pool, Coalmine Beach); the park as a spot must take its own visitor point, not one of theirs.

name: Giant Tingle Tree
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre (largest-girthed living eucalypt, an 800 m circular walk from the Hilltop Road car park); a distinct forest giant.
objection: Shares Hilltop Road with Hilltop Lookout; may be seen as part of one Hilltop drive.

name: Hilltop Lookout
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page and the Walpole Visitor Centre name it (forest-clearing view over the Frankland River, Nornalup Inlet and the Southern Ocean). Case for: two sources and a real view. Case against: rule 3, a short stop on the same one-way Hilltop Road as the Giant Tingle Tree, about 1 km apart; could be folded into that spot.
objection: A ten-minute look on the way to the Giant Tingle Tree.

name: Circular Pool
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (Frankland River pool and rapids, two viewing platforms, boardwalk, picnic area) and the Walpole Visitor Centre names it; a popular picnic and walking stop.
objection: Short visit, mainly a picnic spot.

name: Coalmine Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (family swimming and paddling beach on Nornalup Inlet, picnic area, boat and kayak launch) and the Walpole Visitor Centre names it.
objection: An inlet beach mainly used by those staying at the adjacent holiday park.

name: Irwin Inlet
reason: Rule 1: DBCA site page only (picnic, boating and fishing; sand spit reached by 4WD from Peaceful Bay). Case for: a named DBCA visitor site. Case against: one source, and visitors mostly reach it from Peaceful Bay, which is kept; a quiet fishing spot rather than a draw.
objection: Locals' fishing spot; overlaps Peaceful Bay.

name: Mount Clare
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (summit trail through tingle and karri to Southern Ocean views, picnic area, Deep River loop) and the Walpole Visitor Centre lists it among half-day walks.
objection: Candidate flagged as a disambiguation: confirm it is the Walpole Wilderness Mount Clare (not Albany's Mount Clarence) before pinning.

name: Conspicuous Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page 'Conspicuous Cliff' (limestone cliffs, surf beach, lookouts, whale watching, Bibbulmun day walk to Rame Head) and the Walpole Visitor Centre; 13 km east of Walpole. Keep as one spot under DBCA's name, Conspicuous Cliff.
objection: None strong; name choice (Cliff vs Beach) to settle with the proposer.

name: Granite Skywalk
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Porongurup park page; a suspended walkway on Castle Rock with lookouts to Albany and the Stirling Range, a 4.4 km return walk. Keep as one with Castle Rock (the board lists 'Castle Rock'): duplicate of Castle Rock if that is kept, the skywalk is the named attraction.
objection: Two names for one walk and rock; must not ship as two spots.

name: Devils Slide
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA's Porongurup page lists the Devils Slide walk (5 km, 2 h, highest Porongurup peak, views north and south) and Mountain Country Tourism (Mount Barker's visitor centre) has a trail page; a distinct summit walk.
objection: Shares a trailhead area with the Tree in the Rock circuit; secondary to the Granite Skywalk.

name: Gibraltar Rock
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found no counted source; only climbing guides (UKClimbing) describe it, reached by an unmarked 4WD track and taped path, and DBCA lists no visitor site or trail for it.
objection: A prominent Porongurup monolith with a Wikipedia article; a climbers' crag could be a draw for a niche.

name: Castle Rock Estate
reason: Winery rule: a cellar door named once in a board itinerary PDF, not singled out as a destination in its own right; one of many Great Southern cellar doors.
objection: The board's highlights itinerary does name it, and it has views of the Stirling Range.

name: Mount Trio
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and Stirling Range park page; a steep summit walk to three summits linked by a plateau with a picnic area at the trailhead.
objection: Lesser-known than Bluff Knoll and Toolbrunup; both sources are DBCA.

name: Toolbrunup Peak
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page and park page; the Stirling Range's second-highest peak, a hard scramble with 360-degree views.
objection: Both sources are DBCA; a fit-walkers' summit.

name: Stirling Range Scenic Drive
reason: Rule 1: DBCA's Stirling Range park page names the 42 km mostly unsealed scenic drive through the heart of the park with stops. Case for: the main non-hiking way to see the range, a real half-day outing. Case against: 'a spot is a place': a road, whose stops (peaks, lookouts, picnic areas) are the places; it overlaps the park itself.
objection: Drives are routes, not places; it duplicates the park.

name: Cape Riche
reason: Re-looked: one counted source, Visit Albany's (amazingalbany.com.au) nature-based camping page, which names Cape Riche as a caretaker-run campground; the City of Albany camping page agrees. Case for: a remote cape for fishing, swimming, snorkelling, headland rock walks and Mount Melville. Case against: named only as a campground, no source describes a sight; one source.
objection: A campground listing is not a visitor 'See' entry; mostly anglers and campers.

name: Puntapin Rock
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-golden-outback (4 km south-east of Wagin in the Wheatbelt, per Wikipedia).
objection: Wikipedia cites a Golden Outback holiday planner, so the golden-outback pass may find a counted source.

name: Oyster Harbour
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (swimming beaches, picnic areas, fishing, boat cruises up the Kalgan River). Case for: a counted source naming it as a family outing. Case against: rule 3, the harbour is a water body visited from Emu Point on its southern shore (kept); as a spot it is a near-duplicate of Emu Point.
objection: Its visitor point is Emu Point.

name: King George Sound
reason: Rule 3: a body of water, seen from the places on its shore (Middleton Beach, Emu Point, Torndirrup lookouts, Princess Royal Fortress); no counted source names it as a place to go, and whale-watching tours on it are operators.
objection: A highly viewed article and the setting of Albany's whale watching; its visitor experience is captured by the shore spots.

name: Valley of the Giants
reason: Rule 1+2: Australia's South West board listing and DBCA's Walpole-Nornalup page (Tree Top Walk 40 m up in the tingle canopy, Ancient Empire). Keep as one with 'Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk' (also a board listing): duplicate of that entry, one spot.
objection: Two board listings for the same site; must not ship twice.

name: The Kodja Place
reason: Rule 1+2: Australia's South West board listing and its own site: Kojonup's cultural centre with the Kodj Gallery, Storyplace, Australian Rose Maze and Noongar stories; a real indoor visit. Note: it is in Kojonup, not Albany as the candidate note says (still Great Southern).
objection: One counted source; a small-town centre visitors mostly reach passing through on the Albany Highway.

name: Museum of the Great Southern
reason: Rule 1+2: Australia's South West board listing and the WA Museum's own page: Albany's branch of the state museum on Residency Road, open daily 10-4, free, with the Brig Amity replica and natural and social history galleries. Keep as one with any 'Residency Museum' or 'Brig Amity' candidate.
objection: Candidate coordinates are the WA Museum in Perth (redirect); the pin must be resolved at Residency Road, Albany. Wikivoyage lists the Residency Museum and the Brig Amity separately, a duplication risk.

name: Honeymoon Pool
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west (Honeymoon Pool is in Wellington National Park near Collie, Worsley 6225, per OpenStreetMap).
objection: A popular swimming hole; the south-west pass must cover it.

name: Denmark Animal Farm and Pentland Alpaca Stud
reason: Rule 1: Australia's South West board listing and its own site (animal park, open every day 10-4, WA's first alpaca farm, about 50 alpacas). Case for: a permanent, open, family visitor farm. Case against: rule 2/business: largely a gift shop and petting farm, and the friend test says only if nearby; one source.
objection: A small commercial farm attraction with a shop.

name: Denmark Chocolate Company
reason: Business rule: a chocolate maker and shop, not a place to see.
objection: The board lists it; tastings draw some visitors.

name: Albany Tours
reason: Operator: a tour company, not a place; the places it visits are the spots.
objection: None.

name: Kaarl Wirn Cultural Tours Albany
reason: Operator: an Aboriginal cultural tour operator, not a place; the places it visits are the spots.
objection: Cultural tours are a strong reason to visit; mention them in the destination's text.

name: WOW Wilderness EcoCruise
reason: Operator: a cruise on the Walpole and Nornalup inlets; the place is the inlets (Coalmine Beach and the park are kept).
objection: A well-known Walpole experience; mention it in the place's bio.

name: Whale Watch Western Australia
reason: Operator: a whale-watching company, not a place.
objection: None.

name: The Lake House Denmark
reason: Business rule: accommodation, restaurant and cellar door, not a landmark estate a guide singles out.
objection: The board lists it.

name: Fernhook Falls
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. OpenStreetMap places it in North Walpole, a locality of the Shire of Manjimup, in Mount Frankland South NP.
objection: A clear keep on the merits (DBCA site page and Walpole Visitor Centre); the south-west pass must cover it.

name: East Mount Barren
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page: a 450 m quartzite peak on the Southern Ocean with a summit walk from the western car park and views over the park; a distinct draw near Hopetoun but inside Fitzgerald River NP (Great Southern per the brief).
objection: One counted source; a hard short climb.

name: Lights Beach
reason: Rule 1+2: DBCA site page (beach on the Bibbulmun Track just east of William Bay NP for surfing, fishing, walking and sightseeing); a second-tier Denmark beach a real source names.
objection: Rule 3 risk: close to Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks; the DBCA page sits under Greens Pool.

name: Mandalay Beach
reason: Outside the region: belongs to wa-south-west. DBCA places it in D'Entrecasteaux NP, and OpenStreetMap places it in Broke, a locality of the Shire of Manjimup.
objection: A clear keep on the merits (DBCA, Walpole Visitor Centre, the 1911 wreck); the south-west pass must cover it.

name: Emu Point
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (calm, shallow swimming beach, picnic lawns, fishing, boating, windsurfing) on Oyster Harbour; Wikivoyage Albany names the Middleton Beach-Emu Point path.
objection: Partly a suburb and holiday-park area; it is the visitor point of Oyster Harbour, so the two must not both ship.

name: Peaceful Bay
reason: Rule 1+2: re-looked and found the Walpole Visitor Centre explore page: a coastal village 33 km east of Walpole with turquoise water for swimming, snorkelling and fishing; a second-tier beach village.
objection: One counted source; a holiday-shack village.

name: Mount Romance Sandalwood Factory
reason: Business rule: a sandalwood factory and shop with product tours, named only in an accommodation directory (WA Holiday Guide), not a counted visitor source.
objection: It offers daily information tours, which some visitors take.

name: Plantagenet Wines
reason: Winery rule: a business-directory listing (Mountain Country Tourism) of a cellar door; the region's first winery (1975) but not singled out by a visitor source as a destination in its own right.
objection: Historic as the Great Southern's first winery.

name: Mount Barker Wineries
reason: Not a place: a grouping of the sub-region's wineries (Mount Barker Wine Producers' list); the winery rule keeps only a singled-out estate.
objection: Wine touring is a reason to visit; belongs in destination text.

name: Bornholm
reason: Rule 1/3: a rural locality with no visitor source and nothing named to see; its coast is West Cape Howe NP, judged separately. (Candidate coordinates and views belong to the Danish island.)
objection: None.

name: Wilson Inlet
reason: Rule 1: re-looked and found Tourism WA's attraction page (paddling, kayak and canoe hire, fishing, the 12 km Wilson Inlet Heritage Trail to Crusoe Beach, inlet cruises). Case for: a counted source and a range of things to do. Case against: rule 3, a water body whose visitor points are Ocean Beach (kept) and Denmark's riverfront; the Heritage Trail might be the better spot.
objection: A 20 km water body has no single visitor point; overlaps Ocean Beach.

name: Albany
reason: Rule 1-2: a town with its own Wikivoyage page and Tourism WA's Great Southern page; the region's main base with museums, forts, the whaling station and beaches visitors stay for.
objection: As a city it may be a destination rather than a spot; that is the proposer's call, not a reason to drop it.

name: Denmark
reason: Rule 1-2: a town with its own Wikivoyage page and named on Tourism WA's Great Southern page; visitors base there for William Bay NP, the wineries and Wilson Inlet.
objection: Its headline draws (Greens Pool, Elephant Rocks) are separate candidates, so the town must not become a wrapper for them; it stays only for its own base role and inlet setting.

name: Princess Royal Fortress
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage lists 'The Princess Royal Fortress and National ANZAC Centre' as a paid museum visit of several hours, and the board lists the National ANZAC Centre; one spot for the site (the ANZAC Centre is on it, not a second spot).
objection: Visitors and the board name it the National ANZAC Centre; the proposer should consider that name (or both) so search finds it.

name: Albany Historic Whaling Station
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage and the board list it as a museum with a self-guided tour of the Cheynes IV and flensing decks; a half-day visit.
objection: None of substance; note the Wikipedia title is 'Cheynes Beach Whaling Station', which is a near-name of the separate Cheynes Beach (a different place 60 km east).

name: Old Post Office, Albany
reason: Rule 1-2: one counted source (Wikivoyage See) names it for its spiral tower stair and a museum inside; a heritage building the public can enter.
objection: Wikivoyage also says it now houses restaurants and a weaver; whether the museum is still open is unconfirmed, and with one source and a short visit it is marginal (a building on the Stirling Terrace heritage walk rather than a destination in itself).

name: Desert Mounted Corps War Memorial
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Mount Clarence. The memorial stands at the top of Mount Clarence where Wikivoyage's Mount Clarence Trails begin, and is the same visitor stop (views over the harbour); keep the two as one spot, Mount Clarence, and name the memorial in its bio.
objection: The memorial is the better-known name and the actual standing point (the Anzac dawn service site); the owner may prefer to name the single spot after it instead of the hill.

name: Mount Clarence
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage (Mount Clarence Trails, boardwalk around its base) and the board's Great Southern itinerary name it; summit memorial, trails and harbour views make a 30 min to 2 hr visit. Holds the Desert Mounted Corps Memorial as one spot.
objection: A town hill some would call a local reserve; it survives on the memorial and the views, which is why it absorbs the memorial candidate.

name: Bibbulmun Track
reason: Rule 1-2: a long-distance walk promoted by DBCA, the board and Wikivoyage; walked in day sections around Denmark, Walpole and Albany.
objection: It runs 963 km across three WA regions (Perth Hills to Albany); it must be one spot across the whole run, not one per region, and its pin and region need coordinating with the Perth and South West judges.

name: Munda Biddi Trail
reason: Rule 1-2: a long-distance mountain-bike trail promoted by DBCA, the board and Wikivoyage, ridden in day sections through the tingle and karri forests to Albany.
objection: Like the Bibbulmun it spans several regions, so one spot overall; it is a cycling route used mostly by dedicated riders, a narrower draw than the walking track.

name: The Gap
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA's Torndirrup page and the board ('The Gap and Natural Bridge') name it as a headline sight, with clifftop viewing platforms over the Southern Ocean. Keep as one spot named 'The Gap and Natural Bridge', as DBCA lists them.
objection: It lies inside Torndirrup National Park, which is also kept; the park needs a different visitor point and photo from this spot. (The DBCA site URL in the candidate is a 404; the park page and board listing carry it.)

name: Torndirrup National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA park page and the board list it; Blowholes, Salmon Holes, Misery Beach, Bald Head walk make it a half-day or more beyond The Gap.
objection: Its best-known feature is a separate spot; the park must take another visitor point (Blowholes or Salmon Holes) so it is not a near-duplicate of The Gap.

name: Little Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page and board listing for a sheltered swimming beach at Two Peoples Bay; a second-tier beach a real source names.
objection: Two Peoples Bay Nature Reserve may also be a candidate; if both are kept they need distinct points (Little Beach is the reserve's best-known stop).

name: Fitzgerald River National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA, Wikivoyage and the board list it; a large coastal park with walks, beaches, wildflowers and whale-watching, an obvious draw.
objection: Remote with gravel access from Bremer Bay and Hopetoun; the whole park sits in this region per the boundary brief.

name: William Bay National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA park page and board listing; headlands, Madfish Bay and Waterfall Beach beyond its two famous spots.
objection: Greens Pool and Elephant Rocks are separate spots and are why most visit; the park keeps only a different visitor point (Madfish Bay or Waterfall Beach) and photo. DBCA notes some path closures during works, but the park stays open.

name: Greens Pool
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page, park page and board listing; a sheltered granite-ringed swimming pool, the area's main summer draw.
objection: None of substance.

name: Elephant Rocks
reason: Rule 1-3: DBCA site page and board listing name it separately, a distinct beach and granite formation with its own Wikipedia article and its own walk down.
objection: It is a 10-minute walk from Greens Pool and many visit both in one stop, so it could be argued as part of Greens Pool; DBCA and the board list it as its own site, so it stays separate.

name: Valley of the Giants Tree Top Walk
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page ('internationally recognised nature-based tourism attraction') and the board; a paid 40 m-high walkway in the tingle forest, a headline sight.
objection: None; the Ancient Empire boardwalk at the same site is part of it, not a second spot.

name: Porongurup National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA park page and board listing; granite range with walks, scenic drives and the Tree in the Rock and Devils Slide.
objection: Castle Rock and the Granite Skywalk are a separate spot and its headline; the park needs another visitor point (Tree in the Rock picnic area) to stay distinct.

name: Castle Rock
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page and the board; the Castle Rock walk to the Granite Skywalk, a 2-3 hr walk with range views.
objection: The draw is the Granite Skywalk; the proposer may name the spot 'Castle Rock Granite Skywalk' so visitors recognise it.

name: Stirling Range National Park
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA, Tourism WA and the board; the only major range in southern WA, with peak walks, the Stirling Range Drive and wildflowers.
objection: Bluff Knoll is a separate spot; the park needs a different point (Stirling Range Drive or Mount Trio/Toolbrunup).

name: Bluff Knoll
reason: Rule 1-2: DBCA site page, Tourism WA and the board; the highest peak in southern WA with a summit walk.
objection: None of substance.

name: Albany Town Hall
reason: Rule 2 and 4: an 1887 civic building seen from the street; its only visitor listing (Wikivoyage Do) is as a theatre for plays and concerts, i.e. recurring shows, which are not spots. The candidate carries no counted source of its own.
objection: Wikivoyage does list it and it is one of WA's oldest buildings; if the owner counts a performing venue, it could reach review, but there is nothing to see there outside a show.

name: Mount Trio Bush Camp and Caravan Park
reason: Not a spot: accommodation (a bush camp and caravan park), even though the board lists it.
objection: It sits at the Mount Trio trailhead; the trail or peak, not the camp, would be the spot if a source names it.

name: Cheynes Beach Caravan Park
reason: Not a spot: accommodation (a caravan park). The beach beside it, Cheynes Beach, has its own board listing and is the place to judge.
objection: None: the beach is the place, not the caravan park.

name: Yongernow Australian Malleefowl Centre
reason: Rule 1: two counted sources: Lonely Planet POI page (opened: 'the excellent, community-managed and volunteer-run Yongergnow Malleefowl Centre is in Ongerup') and the Australia's South West board listing, plus the WA Museum WAnderland listing (opened). Rule 2: interpretive centre with displays on the mallee and malleefowl, captive-raising program, gallery and cafe; open Tue-Sat 9am-4pm, paid entry (about A$12 adult). Rule 3: distinct attraction, the only malleefowl centre. Rule 4: permanent venue. Note: the centre's own spelling is 'Yongergnow' (Shire of Gnowangerup, Lonely Planet); use that name.
objection: Small volunteer-run centre in a tiny wheatbelt town; Lonely Planet itself says to check opening hours (closed Sun-Mon and public holidays), and visitors mostly stop in passing between the Stirling Range and Esperance/Ravensthorpe; only if nearby anyway on the friend test.
